arxiv-2009-10576.title: Ethical Machine Learning in Health Care Journal: Xxxx. Xxx. Xxx. Xxx. DOI: 10.1146/((please add article doi))
arxiv-2009-10576.creator: Irene Y. Chen, 1 Emma Pierson, 2 Sherri Rose, 3 Shalmali Joshi, 4 Kadija Ferryman, 5 and Marzyeh Ghassemi 4,6
arxiv-2009-10576.description: Abstract The use of machine learning (ML) in health care raises numerous ethical concerns, especially as models can amplify existing health inequities. Here, we outline ethical considerations for equitable ML in the advancement of health care. Specifically, we frame ethics of ML in health care through the lens of social justice.

arxiv-2012-12772.title: Matrix optimization based Euclidean embedding with outliers
arxiv-2012-12772.creator: Qian Zhang, Xinyuan Zhao, Chao Ding
arxiv-2012-12772.description: Abstract Euclidean embedding from noisy observations containing outlier errors is an important and challenging problem in statistics and machine learning. Many existing methods would struggle with outliers due to a lack of detection ability. In this paper, we propose a matrix optimization based embedding model that can produce reliable embeddings and identify the outliers jointly.

arxiv-2108-07280.title: Quantum Extremal Surfaces and the Holographic Entropy Cone
arxiv-2108-07280.creator: Chris Akers, Sergio Hernández-Cuenca, and Pratik Rath
arxiv-2108-07280.description: Abstract Quantum states with geometric duals are known to satisfy a stricter set of entropy inequalities than those obeyed by general quantum systems. The set of allowed entropies derived using the Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) formula defines the Holographic Entropy Cone (HEC). These inequalities are no longer satisfied once general quantum corrections are included by employing the Quantum Extremal Surface (QES) prescription.

arxiv-2207-07943.title: DESY 19–061, DO-TH 20/09, TTP22–048, RISC Report Series 22–09, SAGEX 20–20, PoS (LL2022) 048 The 3-loop anomalous dimensions from off-shell operator matrix elements This project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under the Marie Sklodowska–C
arxiv-2207-07943.creator: Kay Schönwald
arxiv-2207-07943.description: Abstract We report on the calculation of the three–loop polarized and unpolarized flavor non–singlet and the polarized singlet anomalous dimensions using massless off–shell operator matrix elements in a gauge–variant framework. We also reconsider the unpolarized two–loop singlet anomalous dimensions and correct errors in the foregoing literature.

arxiv-2302-06579.title: AbLit : A Resource for Analyzing and Generating Abridged Versions of English Literature
arxiv-2302-06579.creator: Melissa Roemmele, Kyle Shaffer, Katrina Olsen, Yiyi Wang, Steve DeNeefe
arxiv-2302-06579.description: Abstract Creating an abridged version of a text involves shortening it while maintaining its linguistic qualities. In this paper, we examine this task from an NLP perspective for the first time. We present a new resource, AbLit , which is derived from abridged versions of English literature books. The dataset captures passage-level alignments between the original and abridged texts.

arxiv-2303-04936.title: Degeneracy Loci in the Universal Family of Abelian Varieties
arxiv-2303-04936.creator: Ziyang Gao and Philipp Habegger
arxiv-2303-04936.description: Abstract . Recent developments on the uniformity of the number of rational points on curves and subvarieties in a moving abelian variety rely on the geometric concept of the degeneracy locus. The first-named author investigated the degeneracy locus in certain mixed Shimura varieties.

pmc-10669584.creator: Lauren Sahakian, Ainsley M. Robinson, Linda Sahakian, Rhian Stavely, Mark R. Kelley, Kulmira Nurgali
pmc-10669584.description: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by chronic relapsing inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract. The prevalence of IBD is increasing with approximately 4.9 million cases reported worldwide. Current therapies are limited due to the severity of side effects and long-term toxicity, therefore, the development of novel IBD treatments is necessitated.

pmc-11458305.title: The Effect of “Motivational Interviewing” and “Information, Motivation, and Behavioral Skills Model” Counseling Interventions on the Choice of Delivery Mode in Pregnant Women Using Face-to-Face Training vs. Mobile App: A Randomized Controlled Trial

pmc-11624234.title: Neurophysiological identification and differentiation between the motor and sensory roots in pediatric spinal cord lipoma surgery
pmc-11624234.creator: Katharina Lutz, Timothy Müller, Sebastian Grunt, Cordula Scherer, Martin U. Schuhmann, Mazen Zeino, Sonja Vulcu, Arsany Hakim, Jonathan Wermelinger, Pablo Abel Alvarez Abut, Katarzyna Pospieszny, Andreas Raabe, Philippe Schucht, Kathleen Seidel
pmc-11624234.description: BackgroundRadical resection of spinal cord lipomas reduces the rate of re-tethering. Current conventional neurophysiological mapping techniques are not able to differentiate between crucial motor nerve roots and sensory roots. Enhanced differentiation could contribute to complete resection. We present our experience with a double-train paradigm to differentiate between motor and sensory roots.

pmc-12526649.title: Multiaxial Fatigue Behavior of CFRP Thin-Walled Tubes: An Experimental Study with Analysis of the Acoustic Signals
pmc-12526649.creator: Szymon Duda, Michał Smolnicki, Paweł Zielonka, Paweł Stabla, Grzegorz Lesiuk, Zhanhua Wang
pmc-12526649.description: The fatigue behavior of continuous fiber-reinforced composite materials is still not fully understood, particularly under multiaxial out-of-phase loading conditions. This study assesses the multiaxial fatigue behavior of thin-walled carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) tubular specimens fabricated by filament winding (FW). A comprehensive experimental study is presented, investigating axial-torsion loads, phase shifts (0°, 45°, and 90°), and load ratios (−1, 0.

pmc-12752064.title: Overwinter movement ecology of two Sparrow species in southeastern Ohio
pmc-12752064.creator: Jacob E Morgan, Kelly A Williams
pmc-12752064.description: Anthropogenic development and land use changes, including habitat loss and fragmentation, have resulted in the decline of many North American birds. Overwintering birds need food resources to meet energetic demands, thermal refugia to reduce energetic costs, and cover to avoid predation.

pmc-12784089.title: Trunk-to-limb fat ratio and its relationship with cardiometabolic risk factors in Korean children and adolescents
pmc-12784089.creator: Jong Han Kim, Jun Hong Park, Hae Sang Lee, Young Suk Shim
pmc-12784089.description: Purpose Childhood obesity is a growing global health concern associated with various cardiometabolic risk factors. The aim of this study was to examine the relationships between the trunk-to-limb fat ratio on dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and cardiometabolic risk factors in Korean children and adolescents.

pmc-13191354.title: Impact of Prior Ahmed Glaucoma Valve Implantation on Surgical Success and Prognosis in Eyes Undergoing Keratoplasty
pmc-13191354.creator: Fatma Isil Sozen-Delil, Burak Tanyildiz, Saban Simsek
pmc-13191354.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to evaluate the surgical outcomes and prognosis of patients who underwent Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK) or penetrating keratoplasty (PK) following Ahmed glaucoma valve (AGV) implantation.MethodsPatients who underwent keratoplasty at the cornea department of our hospital between April 2016 and April 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients with a history of prior AGV implantation were included.

pmc-13326651.creator: Xixi Yang, Lixian Chen, Luyao Chi, Yan Wang, Tao-Hsin Tung, Dongjun Bi
pmc-13326651.description: BackgroundPsychological problems among children and adolescents are increasing, and people with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) face varying degrees of stigma as they grow up. Such perceptions of stigma can prevent them from seeking psychological help and adhering to treatment. However, a standardized instrument for assessing ADHD-related stigma in Chinese populations is lacking.

pmc-13353787.title: Drivers of farmers’ intentions to adopt genome-edited cassava resistant to cassava brown streak disease in Uganda
pmc-13353787.creator: Alice Onek Atimango, Stephen Wamala Kalule, Brian Senyange, Wim Verbeke, Hans De Steur
pmc-13353787.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Genome editing has been increasingly promoted as a promising breeding technology to strengthen the agrifood system. However, its success largely depends on farmers’ adoption of the technology, a topic that remains insufficiently addressed in current literature. This study applies the model of goal-directed behavior (MGB) to examine farmers’ adoption intention for genome edited (GE) cassava, resistant to cassava brown streak disease, in a hypothetical scenario in a developing country context.

pmc-13565021.title: ALK Expression Without ALK Rearrangement in EWSR1::ATF1-Fused Inflammatory and Nested Testicular Sex Cord Tumor
pmc-13565021.creator: Min Chong Kim, Hee Jung Kwon, Su Hong Kim
pmc-13565021.description: Inflammatory and nested testicular sex cord tumor (IN-TSCT) is a recently recognized, rare testicular sex cord–stromal neoplasm characterized by a recurrent EWSR1::ATF1 fusion and potentially aggressive clinical behavior. Because of its nested epithelioid morphology accompanied by prominent inflammatory infiltrates, IN-TSCT may be mistaken for seminoma, while frequent diffuse CD30 expression further complicates the differential diagnosis with lymphoma.
